value: NONE, BECAUSE the residual question is not measurable from class-space, and the honest answer is to say so rather than to spec a watch that cannot be emitted. What this seam raises over time is: does a floor that was REPORTED broken actually get FIXED — i.e. does the report reaching Claude close the loop Akien named? That question is answered only by launch records in instance-space (~/.cairn/logs/preflight.json), and the probe berthing doctrine's destination (ii) — an instance-space probe — remains authored doctrine with NO WORKED EXAMPLE (filed by watchme-emits-a-probe, 2026-07-30). Carrying a watch I cannot emit would be exactly the silence the emission gate exists to refuse, wearing a spec's clothes. Two things kept this from becoming an excuse: the ONE residual question that WAS answerable from class-space — 'does the declared dependency set stay true as imports are added?' — was made PHYSICS instead of a watch (test_every_third_party_import_is_declared), because a watch on a question you can already answer is waiting to learn what you could measure; and the instance-space edge is filed below rather than dropped.

PROSE PRECURSOR to the spec above, kept because it is the reasoning the spec was compiled from — with ONE CLAIM CORRECTED rather than quietly swapped. It said this was 'probe berthing destination (ii)'s FIRST WORKED EXAMPLE — an instance-space probe'. THAT IS WRONG, and the way it is wrong is instructive: it reasoned from where the DATA lives (the boot log is in ~/.cairn/, never in git). The rule in cairn/tools/base/probe.py sorts on WHAT IS WATCHED, and what is watched here is the LAUNCHER'S DESIGN — the tool, which every install of this repo gets and every install needs working. So it is destination (i): checked in at launchers/probes/reported_but_unfixed_floor.py, beside the code it watches. Reading instance-space from a class-space berth is not an exception; it is the ordinary shape probe.py describes, where the predicate CLOSES OVER host-local data so only the poke crosses. THE TELL that (ii) was wrong: an instance-space berth is an absolute path in a ticket's spec, so the WATCHME gate would red on every other box that cloned the commons. A rule that places a probe where the gate cannot follow has not placed it. 

The rest stands: launchers/bootstrap.sh + launchers/superclaude write every launch to ~/.cairn/logs/boot through bin/logger_for_bash — what was probed and what came back (`verify:`), every repair attempted with its rc + output (`apply:`), each finding that SURVIVED apply (`report: unfixed —`), the cost, and the final `exec:` line. It SUPERSEDES the 'NONE, BECAUSE' this ticket carried, which was correct when written: the probe genuinely could not be emitted, because there was nothing to emit it WITH. Akien named the missing piece the same day — 'the WATCHME should be INSIDE of the superclaude script... it should log what the script tried, what worked, what didn't' — and building bin/logger_for_bash is what turned an honest refusal into a satisfiable summons.

2026-09-06 (ticket 3feb201c84ea, one status everywhere): no owning_intention; assigned 'launchers/intention+why.json' from the charter its watchme probe (launchers/probes/reported_but_unfixed_floor.py) berths beside — the one reader surfaced it; data repair, no design change.
